skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface another batch owns; the one lead this reading touches (DL-MECH-107) is proposed through a commit candidate instead of an edit.
Nothing in this paper supplies a therapeutic lever for the reference genotype class; forging hypotheses from a nominal or review-level signal would manufacture a lead.
The paper tests no compound, dose or intervention, so there is no molecule for BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; changes are proposed as commit candidates for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
No proposed change narrows or reverses a consolidated baseline claim; the triples are published in the candidate for an auditor to run.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-02: corresponding author Li WD[au] 758 records, 1 intersecting WWOX (this paper); Li WD[au] AND marmoset 1. A population-genomics and psychiatric-genetics group with marmoset colony access (computational WGS analysis plus Sanger/PCR validation, i.e. mixed). Execution of the sequencing is credible; WWOX is a first encounter for the group, and its WWOX interpretation in the Discussion is drawn from cited mouse and human work, not measured.

field_density.note: This is the only WWOX-and-marmoset record in PubMed. No other primate WWOX genetic association exists to replicate or contradict it.

multihop.note: All 65 references enumerated. The five WWOX-direct references (Breton 2021, Hsu 2021, Iacomino 2020, Johannsen 2018, Repudi 2021) are each already identity records in the registries; they enter this paper only in the Discussion as background for the authors' interpretation and supply none of its measurements.

entries.proposition: The WWOX signal is a single-nucleotide association from the LAMP pedigree analysis, not a copy-number finding: the sites above threshold were located mainly in WWOX and PTPN21.
entries.snippet: The sites that exceeded the threshold were mainly located in two protein-coding genes
entries.anchor: Results, Analysis of epileptic marmosets and controls, para 2

entries.proposition: The genotype counts in Table 1 are given as control/case.
entries.snippet: The numbers indicate the number of each genotype in Control group/Case group

entries.proposition: Several WWOX SNPs lie on one haplotype; they are not independent signals.
entries.snippet: Several SNPs in the WWOX gene were confirmed in the same haplotype
entries.anchor: Results, Analysis of epileptic marmosets and controls, para 2

entries.proposition: The deletion enriched in epileptic animals is a KCTD18-like deletion, not a WWOX deletion.
entries.snippet: Notably, the KCTD18-like deletion was enriched in epileptic marmosets of the CLEA pedigree
entries.anchor: Results, Analysis of epileptic marmosets and controls, para 4

entries.proposition: The KCTD18-like deletion association does not survive multiple-testing correction, by the authors’ own statement.
entries.snippet: P-value for KCTD18-like was no longer significant after multiple testing correction

entries.proposition: No SNP reached genome-wide significance; WWOX is offered as a candidate only.
entries.snippet: Although we did not find any signals that reached genome-wide significance

entries.proposition: Controls include unaffected siblings, i.e. related animals; the association is a pedigree-based case-control analysis.
entries.snippet: Unaffected siblings and unrelated unaffected individuals were treated as controls according to the LAMP manual

entries.proposition: The case definition is at least one witnessed handling-evoked seizure.
entries.snippet: Marmosets that exhibited at least one witnessed seizure induced by handling were classified as epileptic marmosets

entries.proposition: The epilepsy type is not established: no ictal EEG was collected.
entries.snippet: we were unable to collect ictal EEG data for identifying the specific type of epilepsy

entries.proposition: Sample size is acknowledged by the authors as limiting reliability.
entries.snippet: Firstly, the relatively small sample size of available marmosets may limit the reliability of our findings.

entries.proposition: Chimerism was handled by an allele-balance filter, and the authors state their data cannot quantify chimerism.
entries.snippet: Variants with an allele balance below 0.25 were excluded to minimize the influence of chimerism.

entries.proposition: The association set used fingernail samples only, split 11/9 (CLEA) and 6/5 (CAS) control/case.
entries.snippet: CLEA: 11 control marmosets/nine epileptic marmosets; CAS: six control marmosets/five epileptic marmosets
